concept: Global Accelerator vs CloudFront: static anycast IPs for API + edge caching
tests: Telling them apart: CloudFront caches static content, Global Accelerator speeds up dynamic traffic and provides static anycast IPs.
expected: CloudFront — caches static assets at edge locations; Global Accelerator — 2 static anycast IPs and routing over the AWS backbone for the API. Triggers: "static anycast IP", "dynamic API", "static assets", "worldwide latency".
why_not: Route 53 latency routing — DNS only, no backbone or static IPs; S3 Transfer Acceleration — for uploads to S3; an ALB in one Region doesn't help global users.
